facts.raw_span: sinus bradycardia with prolonged P-wave duration (180 milliseconds)
sinus bradycardia with prolonged P-wave duration (180 milliseconds)

concepts.why: The patient's ECG findings show sinus bradycardia with prolonged P-wave duration and atrial flutter, which are characteristic of atrial flutter.
The patient's medical history of hypertension, elevated blood pressure, and increased B-type natriuretic peptide levels suggest hypertensive heart disease.
The patient's echocardiography results show left atrial enlargement, which is a common finding in patients with heart disease.
The patient's echocardiography results show mild pulmonary hypertension, which can be caused by various factors, including heart disease and lung disease.
The patient's medical history of kidney insufficiency suggests chronic kidney disease.
